follow_up_findings.issue: Duplicate public payment_received events during callback review and later provider-query confirmation
follow_up_findings.observation: Read-only inspection of the existing local browser fixture found two public payment_received events linked to the same receipt, followed by one delivery.
follow_up_findings.cause: MatchShopPaymentReceipt emitted payment_received for review as well as matched/extra. The callback lacked a trusted payment timestamp, so the first event preceded verified matching.
follow_up_findings.impact: Incorrect public timeline; this fixture had no duplicated receipt, payment amount or delivery.
follow_up_findings.fix: Emit the public payment fact only when the resulting receipt state is matched or extra. Existing matched/extra early returns retain retry idempotence; different provider transactions retain distinct payment events.

regression.red_result: Review and its retry produced two public events; after provider query there were three instead of one.
checks: Identity mismatch publishes no received-payment event; verified recovery publishes exactly one.
Signed callback review and retry publish no event; query confirmation and matching retries publish exactly one.
Distinct extra provider payment retains its own event while fulfillment outbox remains unique.
Retired-buyer receipt remains reviewable with responsibility retained.

follow_up_findings.evidence_boundary: Historical browser screenshots preserve the earlier duplicate timeline and were not retaken. After the fix, a fresh isolated database and current-source HTTP process passed six focused callback/review/reconcile/worker assertions: zero public events during review, then exactly one public event for one matched receipt and one delivery. No historical events were changed or deleted.
